text.目の前に広がる木々をリビングダイニングに取り込んだ、アンティーク家具の似合うヴィ: A renovation at Hiroo Garden Hills, a vintage block that suits antique furniture, bringing the trees in front of it into the living and dining room. A walnut wall running the length of one side draws you from the entrance towards a bright living room in which the green of the trees shows well; the air made by natural materials — lime plaster, wool-linen carpet — and the antiques bought while the family lived in England sit together easily, and time runs slowly. In the bedroom the walls and ceiling are finished in a pale Farrow & Ball water-based paint and the floor is laid in wool carpet, which softens the room. The kitchen, left semi-open with a large serving counter so that the family can talk while looking at the greenery in the window, is walled around so that it does not assert itself in the living room.
text.オーダーで作った淡いグレーのセミオープンのキッチン。ウォールオーブンや大きな配膳: A semi-open kitchen in pale grey, made to order. A wall oven and a large serving counter keep the design uncluttered. The counter gives the family a place to talk while looking at the greenery in the window.
text.寝室の壁と天井は、イギリス製の水性塗料で仕上げました。ビニールクロスと違い、照明: The bedroom walls and ceiling are finished in an English water-based paint. Unlike vinyl wallcovering it takes lighting softly. It is free of the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) harmful to people, and at home it has been used in the restoration of castles. Natural pigments, pale colours, no smell, a smooth finish.
